Title: Driver trapped and killed in eight-vehicle Kota Kinabalu pileup
Article:
KOTA KINABALU: A man was killed after he was trapped in a four-wheel-drive vehicle in a crash involving seven vehicles and a motorcycle at a traffic light junction along Jalan Kolam here this morning.
The 44-year-old victim, who was driving a Toyota Hilux, was pronounced dead at the scene by Health Ministry (MOH) medical personnel.
Jalan Lintas Fire and Rescue Station chief Assistant Senior Fire Officer Noor Sherriyana Bohari said the station received an emergency call at 6.33am before six personnel and a fire engine were dispatched to the scene.
"Firemen used special rescue equipment to extricate the victim, who was trapped inside the vehicle.
"The victim was extricated but was pronounced dead at the scene," she said in a statement today.
She said the victim's remains were handed over to the police for further action.
The operation ended at 7.55am after the scene was declared safe.

Title: Malaysia Smelting faces near-term earnings hit from RHT suspension
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Smelting Corp Bhd is expected to post lower earnings in the near term following the temporary suspension of mining operations at its subsidiary, Rahman Hydraulic Tin (RHT), analysts said.
Apex Securities Bhd estimated that the suspension, which lasted about 4.3 weeks, could reduce Malaysia Smelting's third quarter financial year 2026 (Q3 FY26) net profit by about RM11 million to RM12 million.
In the absence of updated guidance from the company on the precise financial impact, the firm applied its previously established sensitivity framework.
"Based on Q2 FY26 mining segment profit after tax of RM44.1 million before non-controlling interest, we estimate a run-rate impact of about RM3.4 million per week.
"After accounting for Malaysia Smelting's 80 per cent equity interest in RHT, this translates into an estimated RM2.7 million reduction in company-attributable earnings per week of suspension.
"Applying this to the 4.3-week disruption implies a circa RM11 million to RM12 million reduction in Q3 FY26 company net profit, all else equal," it said.
Meanwhile, Public Investment Bank Bhd (PublicInvest) estimated that the suspension could result in quarterly production falling by 30 per cent, with the mining segment potentially incurring a pre-tax loss of about RM20 million to RM25 million.
The firm said this could reduce its FY26 earnings forecast by 15 per cent to 18 per cent.
"However, Malaysia Smelting's tin smelting operations remain unaffected, since it is able to obtain mines, which would partially compensate for the lost volume from RHT.
"Nevertheless, we keep our earnings forecast unchanged, given that tin prices on the London Metal Exchange have been trending upward since early July 2026, pointing to a potential stronger second half of FY26 for the company," it said.
PublicInvest remains positive on both the tin market and Malaysia Smelting's prospects.
It reiterated its "Outperform" call with an unchanged target price of RM3.10 on the stock.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Jamil Khir charged with causing TH to dispose of RM860.3mil assets
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former minister in the Prime Minister's Department Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom was charged at the Sessions Court today with three counts of causing Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH) to dispose of more than RM860.3 million in assets between 2015 and 2017.
Jamil Khir, 65, who was the minister in charge of religious affairs, pleaded not guilty to all three charges before Sessions Court judge Rosli Ahmad.
According to the charges, Jamil Khir allegedly caused TH to dispose of RM860,308,770.51, equivalent to SAR766,062,237, to Al-Rawda Real Estate Development And Projects Management Co Ltd.
Under the first charge, he allegedly caused TH to dispose of RM42,942,074, equivalent to SAR44.17 million.
The second charge involved RM288,172,134.64, equivalent to SAR250,041,622, while the third involved RM529,194,561.87, equivalent to SAR471,848,615.
The offences were allegedly committed at his office at the Prime Minister's Department's religious affairs division at the Federal Government Administrative Centre and the Putrajaya Islamic Complex on April 3, 2015, Dec 14, 2016, and Aug 17, 2017.
Each charge was framed under Section 403 of the Penal Code, which carries a jail term of between six months and five years, whipping, and a fine upon conviction.
Jamil Khir, a former Jerai member of parliament, wore a black suit when he appeared in the dock.

Title: Serian records country's worst API reading at 173
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: IPD Serian recorded the country's highest air pollutant index (API) reading at 173 as of 8am today, remaining in the unhealthy category and showing little improvement from 174 yesterday evening.
This was followed by Sri Aman at 172 and Kuching at 132.
Checks on the Department of Environment's (DoE) air pollutant index management system (APIMS) portal showed that the other areas recording unhealthy readings were in the peninsula.
They were Selangor's Johan Setia at 158 and Cheras (152); Negri Sembilan's Nilai (131) and Seremban (131); Putrajaya (124); and Alor Gajah, Melaka (105).
Meanwhile, 57 areas recorded moderate API readings as of 8am today, with Indera Mahkota, Pahang, recording the highest at 98.
In Sarawak, moderate readings were recorded in Samarahan (98), Sibu (83), Bintulu (75), Sarikei (75), Samalaju (73), Miri (67), Mukah (67), Kapit (62), ILP Miri (59) and Limbang (55).
In Sabah, Politeknik Kota Kinabalu recorded 71, Kota Kinabalu (62), Tawau (61), Kimanis (58), Sandakan (56) and Keningau (54), while Labuan stood at 59.
In Johor, Tangkak and Larkin both recorded 96, followed by Pasir Gudang (94), Kluang (92), Batu Pahat and Pengerang (88), Kota Tinggi (86) and Segamat (84).
In Negri Sembilan, Port Dickson recorded 87, while Bukit Rambai and Bandaraya Melaka recorded 95 and 72 respectively.
In Selangor, Shah Alam recorded 94, Banting (93), Klang (89), Petaling Jaya (88) and Kuala Selangor (80), while Batu Muda, Kuala Lumpur, stood at 85.
In Perak, Seri Manjung recorded 93, Tasek Ipoh (87), Tanjung Malim (81), Pegoh Ipoh (72) and Taiping (65).
On the east coast, Terengganu's Kemaman recorded 89, Kuala Terengganu (69) and Besut (57), while Tanah Merah and Kota Baru in Kelantan recorded 53 and 52 respectively.
In Pahang, Rompin recorded 86, Temerloh (82) and Jerantut (74).
Kedah's Sungai Petani recorded 69, Kulim Hi-Tech (62) and Alor Star (52), while Penang's Minden recorded 79, Balik Pulau (76) and Seberang Perai (73).
Only 2 areas recorded good air quality, with Langkawi, Kedah, at 30 and Kangar, Perlis, at 29.
An API reading of 0 to 50 indicates good air quality, 51 to 100 moderate, 101 to 200 unhealthy, 201 to 300 very unhealthy and above 300 hazardous.
The public can find the latest hourly API readings on the DoE website or via the MyJAS EQMS mobile application.

Title: Firemen rescue 14 trapped by surge of water in Sungai Pertak
Article:
HULU SELANGOR: Firefighters rescued 14 people, including a child, after they were trapped in the middle of a river following a sudden surge of water at Sungai Pertak in Kuala Kubu Baru yesterday.
Selangor Fire and Rescue Department operations division assistant director Ashrul Riezal Asbar said the department received an emergency call at 5.03pm.
He said a team of five personnel, along with a fire engine from the Kuala Kubu Bharu Fire and Rescue Station, was dispatched to the scene.
"The operation commander reported that 14 people were trapped in the middle of the river, comprising 13 adults and one child.
"Duty personnel, assisted by the Batang Kali Volunteer Fire Brigade, used a river crossing technique to bring all victims safely to the riverbank," he said in a statement today.

Title: #NSTviral: Netizens pay tribute to Flying Doctors team after fatal crash
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: "Beautiful memories that you left behind."
Those were the words shared following the deaths of members of the Flying Doctor Service (FDS) team who had dedicated themselves to providing medical care to communities in Sarawak's interior.
In a Facebook post, Irene Philip
shared footage of the team carrying out their duties
and providing treatment to residents in remote areas.
"Your service to the interior communities will always be remembered. Thank you for bringing healthcare, medicine and hope to our people," she wrote in the caption of the video.
The footage showed one of the victims, medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin, carrying out her duties as usual, including examining an elderly resident.
A check of the comments showed many social media users praising the team's dedication and describing their service as an invaluable contribution that would be difficult to forget.
"So heartbreaking to watch this video... Al-Fatihah to Dr Ainul and Captain Zainol... condolences to the families of the assistant medical officer, nurses Debra and Jessie," wrote Miea.
"I'm envious because their passing has allowed all their good and noble deeds to live on, with all of us praying for these heroes and heroines. I hope my own ending will be like theirs too. Al-Fatihah and condolences," Mahathir commented.
"People in the interior must really feel the loss of their doctors," wrote Jessica.
It was reported that a BO-105
helicopter carrying five people,
including its pilot, crashed near Long Lellang Airport in Ulu Baram, Marudi, Sarawak, last Tuesday.
Those killed were pilot Captain Zainol Afiq Bee Sham, 30; medical officer Dr Ainul Baraah Kamaruddin; assistant medical officer Alexson Adit Henry, 31; and nurses Debra Moset, 40, and Jessie Paya Jok, 44.

Title: Three shot dead, 15 wounded ahead of polls in Philippine Muslim enclave
Article:
COTABATO, Philippines: Three people were killed and 15 others wounded as gunfire erupted hours before polls were to open Monday in a semi-autonomous Muslim region of the Philippines set to choose its first elected parliament.
The vote is the culmination of an on-off peace process that began in the late 1990s and established the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region in Muslim Mindanao (BARMM) in the country's far south.
Cotabato police chief Jibin Bongcayao said the shooting took place just before midnight as members of rival political factions jostled for the right to cast their votes first.
"It started as a struggle for position in the queue between two groups," Bongcayao said of the shooting outside a school being used as a polling station in the regional capital.
"It led to shoving, escalated into a fistfight, and eventually gunfire broke out in a crowded area."
Bongcayao added that the men had belonged to rival parties that have emerged from the group that spent decades fighting for regional autonomy in the predominantly Catholic country, the Moro Islamic Liberation Front (MILF).
In a region long marred by political violence and blood feuds between powerful families, a peaceful election would be considered a successful one, party leaders recently told visiting AFP journalists.
Security has been stepped up across the BARMM in recent days, with more than 20,000 security personnel fanning out in voting areas and quick response teams assembled to address potential violence.
Last month, a motorcade carrying the region's interim chief minister – an appointee of President Ferdinand Marcos – was ambushed and peppered with bullets.
In a separate incident, a man died in hospital in the early hours of Monday following an explosion near another polling station. Police are still investigating the cause.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar to deepen Malaysia-India ties during Keralam visit
Article:
KOZHIKODE: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim is scheduled to attend a private programme at Tulah Clinical Wellness here today as part of his working visit to Keralam, the official name used for the Indian state formerly known as Kerala.
Anwar will meet Kerala Chief Minister Pinarayi Vijayan and Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar. Discussions will focus on strengthening Malaysia-Keralam ties and expanding cooperation in trade, investment, tourism, healthcare, and education.
The prime minister will also hold one-on-one engagements with prominent Indian corporate figures to identify new trade, investment, and business opportunities in high-growth sectors.
The engagements in Keralam complement Anwar's broader economic diplomacy in India, following the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi and his bilateral meeting with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi.
They are expected to give fresh impetus to the Malaysia-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership by strengthening business-to-business and sub-national links while opening opportunities for Malaysian firms.
Malaysia and India established diplomatic relations in 1957. India remains Malaysia's largest trading partner in South Asia, with bilateral trade reaching US$18.55 billion (RM79.33 billion) in 2025.
Beyond traditional trade, both nations seek to deepen cooperation in digital technology, education, healthcare, tourism, and investment.
Anwar's meetings with Keralam's political and business leaders aim to broaden the Malaysia-India relationship beyond federal-level ties and create new commercial avenues in one of India's key economic states.
Following his Keralam programme, Anwar departs for the Maldives today for the next leg of his regional diplomatic visit.
On Tuesday, he will receive an official welcoming ceremony at Republic Square in Malé, featuring a 21-gun salute, guard of honour, and cultural procession.
This will be followed by a meeting with Maldivian President Mohamed Muizzu and a delegation meeting at the President's Office.
Anwar will witness the signing of memorandums of understanding between Malaysia and the Maldives, and attend a state banquet hosted by Muizzu.
He will also receive courtesy calls from the Maldivian vice-president, Speaker of Parliament, and Foreign Minister.
Anwar is scheduled to hold an exit press conference with Malaysian media at 4pm local time before departing by boatcade for the airport. His flight will land at the Royal Malaysian Air Force Subang Air Base.
The Maldives leg is expected to strengthen bilateral ties, advance cooperation in areas of mutual interest, and reinforce Malaysia's engagement in the Indian Ocean region.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: "They see me, my face," Rehman on his viral moment with Anwar
Article:
NEW DELHI: "I'm happy, very happy. The people are looking at me. At least they see me. My face, my face is being shown all around the world," said M.Rehman, who played the piano for  Prime Minister, Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim rendition of Kishore Kumar's classic "Khwab Ho Tum Ya Koi Haqeeqat."
The original post on Anwar's X platform has surpassed 1.4 million views and counting. The one minute and 32 second video has since gone viral in India with multiple shares, positive comments and praises on various social media platforms.
However, the moment wasn't an accident but a well prepared 45 years old  pianist meeting his opportunity.
Speaking to Bernama, Rehman who is also a western musical teacher said that he was told about the Prime Minister's stay in the hotel during the 18th BRICS Leaders Summit.
"On Friday, they told me Malaysian Prime Minister might come and that he is fond of Hindi songs. So, I did my research on his favourite songs and told myself I should be able to play whichever song he requests," said Rehman, who has been a pianist for 22 years now.
The next day, during his break, Rehman saw the Prime Minister enter the restaurant area where the piano is placed.
He quickly rushed back to unlocked the piano and began to play.
"The Prime Minister was actually heading elsewhere but he came to me when I started playing, one of his favourite song, Dosh Dosh Na Raha (from the movie Sangam)  and he changed his direction and came to me," said a very delighted Rehman, who described Anwar as friendly and someone who is fond of Hindi Songs.
For many Indians, Kishore's evergreen melodies remain deeply familiar, making the Prime Minister's rendition a pleasant surprise and a nostalgic reminder of the legendary singer's enduring appeal.
Hence, the credit for the viral moment goes to not only Rehman's preparation and his timing but also the song that connected two countries in a single, sincere performance.
The song, from the 1965 Hindi film Teen Devian, is among Kishore's well-loved classics, and Anwar's performance offered an unexpected musical bridge between Malaysia and India. — BERNAMA
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Ex-minister Jamil Khir at KL Courts over Tabung Haji RCI report
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Former Minister in the Prime Minister's Department (Religious Affairs) Datuk Seri Jamil Khir Baharom arrived at the Kuala Lumpur Courts Complex here this morning to face charges linked to the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH).
The 65-year-old former Jerai member of parliament, dressed in a black suit and white shirt, arrived at 7.40am.
He is expected to be charged in the Sessions Court here before Judge Rosli Ahmad at 9am.
Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) chief commissioner Datuk Seri Abd Halim Aman last Thursday confirmed that a former minister would be charged at the Kuala Lumpur Sessions Court today.
He said the prosecution involves a case related to the TH RCI report after the MACC obtained consent from the Attorney-General to bring charges to court.
He added that the MACC recommended three charges under Section 403 of the Penal Code for dishonest misappropriation of property.
Section 403 of the Penal Code provides for an offence against any person who dishonestly misappropriates, converts to their own use, or causes any person to dispose of any property.
Jamil Khir was remanded for five days until Sept 6, before his remand was extended by another two days until Sept 8.

Title: Beyond revenue sharing: Building the fiscal and institutional architecture of one Malaysian production economy
Article:
Samirul Ariff Othman
IF neighbouring states increasingly function as interconnected economic regions, Malaysia must confront a larger question - Does the country possess the fiscal and institutional architecture required to govern such an economy?
For decades, debates on Malaysian federalism have understandably concentrated on constitutional authority, grants, petroleum revenues, development allocations and the distribution of responsibilities between the federal government and the states.
These questions remain important. But redistribution is not the same as integration. A state can receive larger federal transfers yet remain economically disconnected from the rest of the country.
Another can attract billions of ringgit in investment while generating weak linkages with Malaysian suppliers. A third can record high GDP even though the income generated by its productive assets is not proportionately reflected in household welfare.
The next phase of Malaysian federalism must therefore move beyond asking only who receives what. It must also ask how the Federation produces together.
Three Pillars Of Economic Federalism
Malaysia needs to distinguish between three related concepts. Fiscal federalism concerns revenues, expenditure responsibilities and transfers between governments.
Regional planning concerns infrastructure, transport, housing, environmental management and public services whose economic effects frequently cross administrative boundaries.
Production federalism concerns the relationships connecting industries, workers, suppliers, universities, technologies, logistics and investment across states.
Malaysia already practises elements of all three. The problem is that they are insufficiently connected.
Federal budgets may finance infrastructure without systematically measuring the additional production generated across neighbouring states.
Investment incentives may attract factories without adequately determining whether Malaysian suppliers become part of their value chains. State development strategies may compete for similar industries when regional specialisation would generate greater collective value.
An integrated production economy requires all three pillars to reinforce one another. Fiscal federalism finances capability. Regional planning connects geography. Production federalism connects economic activity.
Transfers Cannot Substitute For Productive Capacity
Fiscal transfers remain essential, especially where poorer or geographically disadvantaged states face higher costs in providing roads, schools, healthcare and basic infrastructure.
Indeed, the government's 2027 pre-budget statement explicitly emphasises narrowing regional development gaps while tailoring development strategies to the strengths and potential of individual states and regions.
But transfers alone cannot eliminate structural economic disparities. Where industrial linkages are weak, investment limited, skills inadequate and connectivity poor, additional public expenditure can improve services without necessarily transforming the productive structure.
Fiscal redistribution addresses differences in resources. Production policy addresses differences in economic capability.
Malaysia needs both. The objective should therefore be not merely to compensate regions for being weaker, but to use fiscal policy to strengthen their capacity to produce, connect and specialise.
This suggests several reforms. First, intergovernmental transfers should become increasingly transparent and predictable, with clearer consideration of population, fiscal capacity, infrastructure deficits, geography and the differing costs of delivering comparable public services.
Second, Malaysia should consider Regional Development Compacts between the federal government and participating states around agreed economic objectives.
A northern compact could coordinate semiconductors, advanced manufacturing, water, logistics and talent across Penang, Kedah and adjoining areas.
A southern arrangement could coordinate transport, manufacturing, logistics and housing across increasingly interconnected economic corridors.
Sabah and Sarawak would require arrangements reflecting their distinct constitutional positions, geography and development requirements.
Funding could then support agreed regional outcomes rather than merely collections of isolated projects.
Reward Cooperation, Not Duplication
Federal incentives should also encourage states to cooperate where benefits cross borders.
Suppose Penang and Kedah jointly develop technical training serving semiconductor companies in both states. Or Selangor and Negri Sembilan coordinate industrial transport infrastructure.
Or regional logistics investments in East Malaysia reduce supply-chain costs across multiple jurisdictions.
Projects producing demonstrable cross-border spillovers should qualify for stronger federal support.
The principle is straightforward: Where economic benefits cross state boundaries, fiscal incentives should encourage governments to behave accordingly. This requires better measurement.
Malaysia's national Input-Output tables already show how industries purchase inputs from and supply outputs to one another.
But conventional state GDP cannot adequately show how production in one Malaysian region depends upon another. Regional Input-Output analysis could.
How much of Penang's electronics output depends upon Kedah? How much of Sabah's economy purchases inputs from Peninsular Malaysia? How much of Sarawak's industrial value remains within Sarawak?
Which regions possess strong Malaysian backward linkages, and which rely heavily upon imported intermediate inputs? Where are the largest leakages from domestic production chains?
These are not academic questions. They determine whether an investment creates a wider Malaysian multiplier or remains largely an economic enclave.
DOSM already records interregional merchandise trade between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.
The statistical foundations therefore exist for progressively deeper analysis. Regional and ultimately interregional Input-Output frameworks should become regular instruments of national development planning.
Institutions That See Beyond State Borders
Data alone, however, cannot solve coordination failures. Malaysia should consider permanent Regional Production Councils for its major economic corridors.
These should not constitute another layer of government or assume powers belonging constitutionally to federal or state authorities.
They should be coordinating institutions bringing together relevant ministries, state governments, investment agencies, infrastructure providers, universities and industry.
Their purpose would be practical. Is industrial land being developed without sufficient water or electricity?
Are universities training workers without reference to emerging regional demand? Are ports, railways and highways being planned independently? Are neighbouring states using public resources to duplicate essentially identical industrial clusters? Regional institutions should identify and resolve precisely these failures.
Federalism As Economic Architecture
Federalism is therefore more than a political arrangement governing the distribution of authority.
It is also economic architecture. Malaysia contains markedly different regional economies. The Klang Valley is services-intensive and highly urbanised.
Northern Malaysia contains one of Southeast Asia's important electronics and semiconductor concentrations. Johor is expanding around manufacturing, logistics and integration with Singapore.
Sabah and Sarawak possess different combinations of resources, geography, infrastructure constraints and development opportunities.
Uniform policy therefore has limits. But complete decentralisation has limits too.

Title: Analysts: Umno keeping 'strategic' options open ahead of GE16
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Umno's continued presence in the unity government should not be read as merely buying time, but as a deliberate accumulation of strategic options while the party rebuilds its organisational strength.
Universiti Malaya senior lecturer Dr Mohammad Tawfik Yaakub said Umno was not buying time, as some may think.
"The party wants to enjoy the stability and political resources of being in government while ensuring it is not automatically tied to Pakatan Harapan when elections come," he said, adding that these "strategic options" included access, machinery and political capital.
[[nid:1532237]]
He said leaving the government now would carry significant risks, including losing these advantages and being perceived as a destabilising force.
Meanwhile, International Islamic University Malaysia political scientist Associate Professor Dr Syaza Shukri said there was now little doubt about where Umno was headed in terms of electoral cooperation.
"But (Umno president Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi) saying Umno will stay with the government till end of term signals that they could use all the time they can get to iron out things like seat negotiations and leadership arrangements with Pas."
She said an Umno-Pas pact would likely deliver electoral success, but raised a more pointed question about the internal balance of such an arrangement.
"Definitely working with Pas would bring victory to the pact. But the question is who will gain more — Pas or Umno?"
Tawfik said the dual posture of seemingly criticising PH while remaining in the unity government remained institutionally sustainable for now, as Umno was distinguishing between administrative cooperation and electoral cooperation.
However, he said the strategy had a clear expiry date.
[[nid:1532236]]
"Hardline supporters may ask why the party continues to remain in a government it so openly criticises.
"Fence-sitting voters, meanwhile, may see Umno as inconsistent — enjoying the privileges of government while distancing itself whenever a policy proves unpopular."
On whether there would be an electoral pact in the impending Melaka election, Syaza said Umno had likely not yet made a final strategic decision.
She said this was because the state election would set the template for the rest of the country, making any premature commitment potentially costly.
"Say Umno says they won't compromise on the 21 seats (they had won previously) — are they okay with Pas saying the same thing up north? Where is the line and balance?"
Syaza said the data pointed towards Pas being in a position to claim more seats in Melaka, and that a Umno-PH arrangement would effectively reduce PH to a junior partner.
Also, she said, embracing PH could be framed as abandoning the so-called spirit of Malay-Muslim unity.
"But the assembly seems to direct us towards a Pas-Umno cooperation," she said.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Nestle Malaysia strengthens support for paddy farmers
Article:
Faiqah Kamaruddin
JITRA, Kedah: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd has invested more than RM6 million in its Nestle Paddy Club (NPC) since 2012, as it seeks to strengthen its local rice supply chain while improving productivity and livelihoods among paddy farmers.
Nestle Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the investment covers not only financial support but also farming methods, agricultural inputs, machinery and technical expertise.
"It is many years of investment. I would say it's around RM6 million-plus, but the operation is not just money.
"It is also methods, practices, providing the right variety of rice and sharing all the necessary knowledge through experts," he said during a media familiarisation trip to the NPC here.
The programme currently involves about 200 farmers cultivating more than 600 hectares across Kedah and Perlis.
For the first planting season of 2026, it involved 157 farmers across about 475 hectares and is expected to supply 2,800-3,000 tonnes of rice for Nestle's Cerelac infant cereals this year.
NPC farmers have consistently recorded yields above the national average, with farmers achieving an average of 5.4 tonnes per hectare in the January-February 2025 harvest and 4.96 tonnes per hectare in August-September 2025, compared with the national annual average of about four tonnes per hectare.
For paddy farmer Md Nasir Md Saman, 61, the programme provides support in the form of technical advice, pesticides, vitamins and machinery, including paddy harvesters, land levellers and tractors.
He said crop losses caused by natural disasters are typically covered by assistance from the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada).
"Some farmers also take out paddy insurance. They pay for the insurance, and if a disaster occurs, such as flooding that submerges the crop, Mada will assess the damage and provide compensation. They will provide up to 50 per cent, depending on the extent of the damage," he said.
Another paddy farmer, Zalifah Desa, 54, said the programme had helped lift her productivity and income.
Having farmed paddy since she was 20, Zalifah said her yield had increased to about two tonnes per plot from 1.5 tonnes previously, while income rose to more than RM3,000 per plot from about RM2,000.
Nestle Malaysia business executive officer for nutrition Yeoh She Shiang said the programme was established to secure rice that meets more stringent quality and safety requirements for infant nutrition.
"Our vision was actually to get the highest-quality rice into our Cerelac products, which are made for babies from six months old.
"We wanted to establish a more stringent quality standard that is suitable for babies, which we call 'baby grade', and is higher than the standard for adult consumption," she said.
She said nutritional fortification was added specifically for babies from six months old to support their healthy growth and development.
Nestle Malaysia has sourced 100 per cent of the white rice used in Cerelac locally since 2012, with the rice processed into the infant cereal in Malaysia.
The company is also expanding the programme's sustainability focus, with farmers adopting the Semi-Aerobic Rice Intensification method, which has reduced irrigation water use by about 30 per cent to 40 per cent while maintaining productivity.
The NPC forms part of Nestle Malaysia's wider Farmer Connect programmes, which support local production of paddy, chilli, coffee and cocoa.

Title: Question over NorthEast's capacity constraint despite photonics opportunities coming its way
Article:
Diyana Isamudin
KUALA LUMPUR: NorthEast Group Bhd is still confident of chalking double-digit growth level for the financial year ending Sept 30, 2027 (FY27), as it secures more orders from its customers in the photonics, semiconductor and electrical and electronics (E&E) industries.
This is despite the fact that it is facing facility constraints as the development of its new manufacturing facility, that would expand its production space by 72 per cent, is being delayed due to regulatory hurdles.
The Penang-based precision engineering manufacturer is also confident of reaching record revenue for the current financial year ending Sept 30, 2026 (FY26), as it gains more orders from its existing customers.
"We have been in this business for over 20 years. We have encountered a lot of challenges, and each time we can overcome them," says its chief marketing officer and executive director Yin Thien Hee in an exclusive interview with Business Times.
"To achieve a double digit growth for the next fiscal year, seems possible with additional capacity in the pipeline, where we have expanded our production floor by acquiring a warehouse where we will move our secondary process to," he adds.
NorthEast manufactures mechanical systems and critical components used in photonics applications, including optical circuit switches (OCS), which facilitate high-speed data transmission in data centres.
In anticipation of an increase in demands for OCS, NorthEast has prepared space in its existing facilities for additional computer numerical control (CNC) machines.
According to Yin, 10 more CNC machines have been installed, while another 15 are on the way, that shall be in operation in stages between October and December this year.
"We have three factories (including a warehouse), so we have made necessary adjustments to accommodate fewer machines, which can mitigate the production capacity issue," he says, adding that NorthEast is also subcontracting some of the less complex jobs.
In the third quarter ended June 30, 2026 (Q3 FY26), NorthEast recorded a 39 per cent increase in profit after tax (PAT) and net profit to RM9.85 million, while its revenue rose by 35 per cent year-on-year (YoY) to RM42.85 million.
Its PAT and net profit more than doubled in the nine-month period ended June 30, 2026 to RM29.38 million compared with the preceding year, as its gross profits jumped 61 per cent, due to higher revenue, improved operational efficiency and manpower productivity.
Orders for OCS, primarily from "Customer L" – a global producer of the device that establishes direct photonic connections between endpoints without requiring optical-electrical-optical conversion – is expected to contribute double digit percentage to the group's revenue next year, says Yin.
The order book is expected to exceed RM100 million over the next 12 months, although management has not provided a firm target, he says, adding that NorthEast has sufficient capacity for OCS Production and does not face any delivery issues.
"The other contingency plan we have is looking for a second source for the powder coating sector. No problem with machining wise, but in the second process we are considering adding one more supplier to mitigate the capacity at our major subcontractor," says Yin.
Companies like NorthEast, who manufacture precision engineered products for global E&E component producers, have been increasingly linked with the possibility of becoming alternative sites to those in China.
This comes as the United States (US) is rumoured to be including optical transceivers produced in China under the Covered List of hardware components facing tighter authorisation requirements to be imported into the US.
The US Federal Communications Commission has already updated its Covered List, and optical transceivers are not included as one of the photonics products that requires tighter authorisation to be imported into the country.
However, the risks of the US imposing tighter control over imports of optical transceivers are still there, leading to global producers searching for alternative sites to China. This includes "Customer L", which is now collaborating with NorthEast to produce OCS.
The Penang-based NorthEast is targeting double-digit sales growth in the next financial year, supported by an order book of more than RM80 million.
In Q3 FY26, photonics contributed 37 per cent of NorthEast's revenue, while the E&E and semiconductor segments each accounted for 22 per cent.
The rapid expansion of AI and data centres was driving demand for faster and more efficient data transmission, creating opportunities for companies involved in photonics and precision engineering.
"As AI applications and data centre infrastructure continue to expand, the need for higher data transmission capacity and connectivity is expected to support the broader photonic industry," says Yin.
FACTORY DELAY TESTS CAPACITY
Northeast had originally earmarked RM40 million from its initial public offering proceeds for the third factory, which was slated to accommodate about 200 CNC machines.
The company is assessing the potential impact of the delay and working closely with the state government and relevant authorities to resolve the outstanding regulatory matters and secure the necessary approvals.
At the same time, NorthEast is considering buying another factory if a suitable opportunity arises, says Yin. The group's existing factory utilisation stood at about 81 per cent.
SEMICONDUCTOR OPPORTUNITIES
NorthEast has begun working with two new semiconductor customers, supporting front-end equipment makers, with samples having been fabricated, and submitted for certifications by the customers.
If the samples are certified by the new semiconductor customers, they could contribute a meaningful portion of NorthEast's sales, says Yin. For this venture, the group has committed several million ringgit in capital expenditure.
"The component will be used in a very high-end semiconductor equipment. The stability of the machine will ensure consistent results. It will reduce rejection rates and increase output," he says.
As at end-Q3 FY26, NorthEast's balance sheet remains strong, with low net gearing of 0.04 times, and healthy current ratio of 9.5 times.
Its balance sheet also compares favourably with peers such as Kobay Technology Bhd, which had net gearing of 0.2 times and a current ratio of 1.7 times, and SFP Tech Holdings Bhd, with net gearing of 0.2 times and a current ratio of 1.8 times.
Analysts covering the stock are optimistic of its prospect, given the resilient demand from the photonics segment, gradual recovery in the broader semiconductor cycle and NorthEast's increasing monetization of its indirect AI exposure.
"We believe MNCs would be incentivised to shift a greater share of production allocation towards non-China suppliers such as the group (NorthEast) in Malaysia, reinforcing already sticky relationships and lengthening the customer runway," states Tradeview Research.
The research firm assigned a 'Buy' call on NorthEast with a target price of RM1.34, based on FY27 forecast (FY27F) price-earnings (PE) ratio of 23 times.
Meanwhile, UOB KayHian also assigned a 'Buy' call on NorthEast, with a target price of RM1.42, based on 25 times FY27F PE. The research firm expects NorthEast's FY26 net profit to rise 57 per cent.
"NorthEast is increasingly monetising its indirect AI exposure, having progressed from first-article qualification to mass production of precision-engineered components embedded in AI infrastructure.
"This is spearheaded by its positioning within the supply chain of a contract manufacturer, serving a key US optical solutions provider to the world's leading GPU player.
"With optical demand accelerating and the customer relationship deepening, order momentum is building, providing visibility for a multi-year growth runway potentially extending through 2027," states UOB KayHian in a report.
While the wind of trade and investment seems to be blowing towards Southeast Asia, can NorthEast capture the opportunity without significant production capacity expansions?

Title: Jet fuel surge adds RM7.5bil to MAG costs, Malaysia Airlines fares rise 30pct
Article:
Rafhanah Hazirah Ramlin
KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) is facing up to RM7.5 billion in additional costs following a surge in jet fuel prices after the outbreak of conflict in the Middel East in late February.
MAG group president and chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A Bakar said every US$1 increase in oil prices affects the group's financial performance by about RM50 million.
Jet fuel prices, which were below US$100 a barrel in the first two months of 2026, surged to about US$227 after the conflict began on Feb 28.
He said MAG was profitable in the first two months of the year before the sharp increase in fuel prices put significant pressure on operating costs.
"During the first two months, we recorded a profit. However, after the war began, fuel prices more than doubled.
"For Malaysia Airlines' scale of operations, every US$1 increase in jet fuel prices affects our financial performance by about RM50 million," he said in an exclusive interview with Berita Harian.
Based on the increase from below US$100 to about US$227 a barrel, Nasaruddin estimated the additional cost impact on MAG could reach RM7.5 billion.
He said the cost pressure was expected to weigh on MAG's financial performance in 2026, despite group revenue rising about 19 per cent from a year earlier.
"Our revenue is higher than last year, by about 19%. However, costs have increased at a faster pace than revenue," he said.
Flights Cut To Contain Costs
To manage rising costs, Malaysia Airlines has reduced flights on routes that are no longer profitable.
Nasaruddin said the cuts account for about 5% of total flights, or around 8,000 flights this year.
"We are reducing unprofitable routes and managing costs as much as possible.
"We have also stopped non-essential spending. Besides reducing flights, MAG is using measures such as fuel surcharges and fuel hedging to reduce the impact of oil price volatility," he said.
However, he said the measures had yet to fully offset the increase in fuel costs.
"Whatever we are doing now is still not enough to fully absorb the increase in fuel prices. Costs remain higher," he said.
Malaysia Airlines Fares Rise 30pct
The cost pressures have also contributed to an overall increase of about 30 per cent in Malaysia Airlines' ticket prices for both domestic and international flights.
Nasaruddin said fares were not determined by fuel costs alone, as they also depended on dynamic pricing based on supply and demand.
He said fares could rise when demand was strong, while higher fuel costs could require airlines to impose surcharges to recover part of the additional expenses.
Markets recording stronger demand and higher fares include Europe, particularly London, as well as Australia, New Zealand and India.
However, he said Malaysia Airlines would continue to support travel between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak by maintaining certain fare limits.
Fares Could Stabilise
Nasaruddin said fares could stabilise if oil prices decline after the conflict ends, although the timing of any recovery remained difficult to predict.
"Oil prices move in cycles. Before the war, they were below US$100 a barrel. Now they are around US$160 to US$165.
"If the conflict ends, we expect some stability," he said.
MAG's cost pressures mirror a wider airline industry squeeze as surging jet fuel prices force carriers to raise fares, impose fuel surcharges and trim capacity.
Singapore Airlines, Scoot, Cathay Pacific, Thai Airways, AirAsia X and Cebu Pacific reportedly have all taken pricing measures, while some airlines have also cut flights to contain costs.
Cathay Pacific reportedly raised fuel surcharges by 34 per cent from April and Thai Airways lifted fares by 10-15 per cent.
Budget carrier AirAsia X also adjusted fares, while Cebu Pacific raised fares by 20-26 per cent for several months to offset higher fuel costs.
The fuel shock is also prompting airlines to cut capacity.
AirAsia planned to reduce seat capacity by up to 25 per cent, while Ryanair cut its passenger forecast and winter capacity as fuel costs remain elevated.

Title: Give SMEs a safe voice against cartels, MyCC urged
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR:  enforcement powers for the Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) must come with safe reporting channels, as  small businesses often fear repercussions for complaining against major suppliers.
SME Association of Malaysia president Dr Chin Chee Seong said the association could consolidate anonymous feedback and raise common issues with MyCC on behalf of  members.
"We urge MyCC to investigate cases involving essential supplies swiftly and monitor unusual price movements rather than wait for formal complaints," he said.
"Strong laws without timely enforcement will not bring results. The real success of these changes are a fairer, more competitive business environment."
[[nid:1532222]]
Chin said educating small businesses is vital to effective enforcement, as small and medium enterprises (SMEs) face higher prices and unfair terms from cartels and dominant suppliers because of their weaker bargaining power.
He said  price-fixing and market-sharing raise costs for small firms, which are then passed on to consumers.
"Stronger powers for MyCC are important, but that is only the first step. The most important issue is enforcement."
He said MyCC must act quickly against anti-competitive behaviour, adding that many SMEs are afraid to lodge complaints against major suppliers whom they depend on.
Chin said SMEs want competition based on price, quality and service.
He said many micro and small businesses also risk breaching the Competition Act  because they do not fully understand it.
"While normal trade group discussions on costs or labour are fine, agreeing on prices, discounts or market allocation is illegal.
"Enforcement must go together with education, so  businesses do not unknowingly cross the line."
Chin said stronger MyCC powers would not immediately lower SME costs, as businesses  face higher wages, utilities, rentals and taxes.
However, he said effective enforcement against cartels would create a fairer market.
Chin also called on MyCC to work with business groups to conduct workshops and roadshows nationwide.
He advised business owners to make independent decisions on pricing, discounts and strategy, and avoid sharing commercially sensitive information with their competitors.
Economist Geoffrey Williams said empowering MyCC to tackle monopolies and cartels would enhance competition, improve customer service and lower consumer prices.
[[nid:1532221]]
He said stronger regulatory oversight would force companies to become more agile, innovative and efficient to protect their market share from new competitors.
Williams said direct intervention against cartels must be paired with policy reform, as some cartels exist because of government licensing.
"Removing those licences is essential to tackling cartels and monopolies directly."
He said prices in competitive markets fluctuate with supply and demand, while cartel-controlled prices could remain unchanged even during periods of excess supply.
"Cartel behaviour is also evident when competing brands adjust prices simultaneously rather than independently to attract customers."
On penalties, Williams said higher fines would serve as a deterrent and should not be passed on to consumers, warning that firms attempting to shift penalty costs to customers should face further punishment.
However, he said structural reform, rather than financial penalties, should be the primary driver of market reform.
"The real impact should not be from fines. It should be from removing barriers to entry, such as licences and concessions, and opening market access to anyone who wants to sell products or services."
He said  online cartels cannot easily control the market as long as buyers have choices and sellers aren't locked into one app.
"Digital platforms actually boost competition rather than create monopolies."
He added that tougher competition rules would also attract foreign investors, provided regulations are enforced fairly and do not discriminate against foreign suppliers.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: MyCC: Stronger enforcement aims to protect fair competition
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Corporate Malaysia should not view amendments to the Competition Act 2010 as anti-business, as they target anti-competitive practices rather than large, successful companies.
Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) chairman Tan Sri Idrus Harun said the legal overhaul targets anti-competitive conduct such as cartels, price-fixing, market sharing, bid rigging and abuse of dominant positions that distort competition in the market.
He said the amendments  were aimed at curbing anti-competitive practices that drive up the cost of living.
The 34-clause bill significantly expands MyCC investigative and enforcement capabilities.
Idrus said strong and credible competition enforcement builds investor confidence by providing clear rules and ensuring enterprises compete on merit.
"A level playing field, regulatory certainty and competitive market are important elements of a healthy and attractive investment environment."
On concerns over MyCC's expanded enforcement authority, Idrus said stronger powers would be balanced by strict accountability and procedural safeguards.
Idrus said affected businesses would retain the right to respond to MyCC cases, make formal representations and appeal against MyCC's decision through established channels.
"At the same time, stronger enforcement powers must come with proper safeguards and accountability. The statutory amendments establish a more flexible and proportionate enforcement toolkit, including settlement frameworks and voluntary undertakings."
Idrus urged  boards and  management teams to treat competition compliance as a core element of risk management and corporate governance, rather than acting only after legal issues arise.
He advised enterprises to review commercial agreements, conduct staff training and put systems in place to detect potential competition risks early.
"MyCC and the business community must work as partners rather than adversaries. We should not see each other as being on opposite sides.
"Businesses can work with MyCC through consultation, market reviews, constructive engagement and compliance efforts.
"We should share the same objective: an economy where businesses can invest and innovate, small and medium enterprises  can compete and grow, and consumers benefit from better prices, greater choice, quality and innovation."

Title: Houthis say Saudi Arabia launched over 50 strikes against them in 24 hours
Article:
SANAA: Yemen's Houthis said Sunday that Saudi Arabia had launched more than 50 strikes against their positions in 24 hours, after the Iran-backed group claimed a rare drone and missile attack on a military base in the kingdom.
The Houthis have been engaged in renewed fighting with Saudi-backed government forces since Yemen's civil war reignited in July, when the group declared a maritime blockade on Saudi Arabia and began targeting its ships in the Red Sea.
The latest clashes follow a week-long Houthi offensive that culminated in the group capturing Yemen's Red Sea coast, cementing their hold on the Bab al-Mandab Strait.
The waterway is a vital artery for Saudi oil exports as the Strait of Hormuz remains closed amid the US-Iran war.
Yayha Saree, the group's military spokesman, said "the criminal Saudi enemy has carried out 58 airstrikes in the past 24 hours" in a post on Telegram.
The Houthis carried out their heaviest missile and drone attack in years this week against Saudi Arabia, setting oil sites ablaze and wounding 73.
The group's Almasirah TV channel reported on Sunday that "Saudi aviation carried out two strikes" on Saada, a stronghold for the group.
It also reported artillery fire in the border district of Monabbih, in the same province.
Later on Sunday, Almasirah reported two Saudi strikes on a market in the northern Al-Jawf province.
The Houthis have reported more than 100 strikes against their positions since Tuesday, with no confirmation from Riyadh so far.
Up to now, the strikes have mainly focused on the front lines, in support of Yemeni government forces, without targeting the Houthis' heart of power, including the capital Sanaa.
Yemen's civil war began in 2014 when the Houthis seized the capital and forced out the internationally recognised government.
They then fought a Saudi-led coalition from 2015 until a UN-brokered ceasefire in 2022. The conflict had since been dormant before it roared back to life in July.
TENS OF THOUSANDS DISPLACED
Riyadh says little about the Houthi strikes on its territory, but issues brief alerts almost daily warning of potential attacks in southern regions near Yemen.
On Sunday, the Saudi civil defence agency sent alerts for the city of Abha and the region around Khamis Mushait, and again quickly lifted them.
Earlier in the day, the Houthis said they used drones and missiles to attack the Sharurah military base in southern Saudi Arabia.
The attack targeted "weapons depots and command and control centres that are managing the aggression against our nation and people", Houthi military spokesman Yahya Saree wrote on X.
Late on Saturday, the Saudi civil defence agency had said two people were injured after a projectile fired by the Houthis fell in the Jizan region, which also lies along the border.
The fighting in Yemen in recent weeks has displaced nearly 86,000 people, a UN agency said on Sunday, with the number surging by 10,000 from a day earlier.
The International Organization for Migration added that some of those displaced have begun fleeing Yemen altogether, saying that more than 2,000 people had reached Djibouti.
Yemen's civil war has killed hundreds of thousands of people and triggered a major humanitarian crisis.
The renewed hostilities kicked off in July when the Houthis let an Iranian plane land in defiance of Saudi control of Yemeni airspace.
The government retaliated by striking Sanaa airport, an attack the Houthis blamed on Saudi Arabia.
Yemen is the latest country to be drawn into the broader Middle East war, which began with US-Israeli strikes against Iran in late February.
US news site Axios reported that Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed Bin Salman twice called US President Donald Trump to request strikes on the Houthis last week, but that the request was rejected.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Stronger law gives MyCC edge against cartels [WATCH]
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: Recent amendments to the Competition Act 2010 give the Malaysia Competition Commission (MyCC) more powers and tools in the battle against cartels, bid rigging and price-fixing.
MyCC chairman Tan Sri Idrus Harun said the amendments, which include expanded investigative powers, a settlement framework and a clear court appellate process, were essential to keep pace with evolving market tactics and sophisticated cartel operations.
He said the 34-clause amendment must remain dynamic to address modern challenges.
"Legislation should not be static. As we enforce the law over time, we notice ambiguities and loopholes that perpetrators exploit," he told the
New Straits Times
.
"Cartel operations have moved beyond physical meetings to digital channels like encrypted messaging apps. Perpetrators are always several steps ahead of us."
In July, the Dewan Rakyat passed the Competition Commission (Amendment) Bill 2026, which expands MyCC's powers, strengthens governance and enhances enforcement capabilities.
Domestic Trade and Cost of Living Minister Datuk Armizan Mohd Ali said the legal changes will expand MyCC's role beyond investigating unfair practices, allowing it to study industries and recommend policies to keep markets fair.
"The objective of these amendments is to strengthen MyCC so that it can function more effectively in ensuring a fair and competitive market ecosystem amid increasingly complex cartel activities."
Idrus said a central feature of the overhaul was closing a legal gap involving industry associations.
"Previously, trade bodies used legal technicalities to evade liability by claiming they were not enterprises directly engaged in commercial activity.
"We lost cases in the past because associations argued they are not enterprises or that their conduct does not fall within the definition of an 'agreement' under the act, even though they facilitated cartel conduct among their members."
He said the expanded definitions of agreement and enterprise ensure that trade associations can now be formally investigated and held accountable for facilitating or becoming the conduit for anti-competitive conduct.
The amendments also grant MyCC mandatory powers under the new Section 11A to gather data and documents from commercial entities and statutory bodies during market reviews.
Idrus said  unlike formal investigations into specific errant firms, market reviews are a soft enforcement approach that allows MyCC to understand how a market operates and identifies structural or regulatory issues that affect competition in the market.
"The outcome of a market review will be used by MyCC to make recommendations and advise the government accordingly on competition matters."
To resolve cases faster and reduce lengthy litigation, the updated law introduces a settlement mechanism under Section 38A.
Enterprises that admit liability after a proposed decision can receive up to a 40 per cent reduction in financial penalties.
This fast-track procedure encourages early resolution, helping to correct anti-competitive market behaviour quickly so that consumers benefit without waiting years for prolonged legal battles.
Idrus said the law also incorporated explicit informant protection and financial reward provisions under Sections 64A and 64B to encourage whistleblowers to expose cartels and bid-rigging schemes.
"Our ultimate goal is to protect consumer interests and promote healthy economic development."
"These amendments give us the necessary legal tools to ensure fairness and transparency at every level.
"Under the law, companies that engage in anti-competitive conduct can be fined up to 10 per cent of their global turnover during the period of infringement."
Up to Aug 17, MyCC had imposed RM667.3 million in total financial penalties across 16 final infringement decisions involving 270 companies, signalling a mounting crackdown on anti-competitive corporate behaviour.
MyCC enforcement actions span critical sectors of the economy. The 16 final infringements issued so far cover numerous industries, such as transportation, agriculture, food and beverage, logistics, education and construction.
MyCC is pursuing 13  investigations — 12 targeting bid-rigging schemes and one focused on price-fixing.
These ongoing probes involve more than 500 companies linked to public and private tenders valued at over RM4.34 billion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Oman says Hormuz talks with Iran, Gulf states postponed
Article:
MUSCAT: Oman has announced the postponement of a meeting Monday between Iran and Gulf countries on the Strait of Hormuz, the major flashpoint in the Middle East war.
Iran's foreign ministry had said there would be a meeting hosted by Oman where the future of the strait, vital for global oil and gas flows, would be negotiated.
Tehran said Iraq and Gulf countries would take part, without specifying which states, but no country in the region had confirmed its participation while Bahrain ruled out attending.
"It has been decided to postpone to a later date the regional meeting that was to be held on Monday in Salalah, in order to create conditions conducive to a constructive dialogue," the Oman News Agency said on Sunday.
Omani Foreign Minister Badr Albusaidi said on X that "we remain determined to promote dialogue that contributes to stability and lasting cooperation in our region."
The Strait of Hormuz has been subjected to an Iranian and a later US blockade since February 28 when the US and Israel launched strikes on Iran, prompting a wider war across the region.
A June accord between Washington and Tehran faltered on disagreements over Hormuz, and a blistering offensive in recent days by Yemen's Houthi rebels has given the Tehran-allied group leverage over a second critical waterway, the Bab al-Mandab.
More than six months into the Middle East war, the Hormuz blockade continues to drive up oil prices, which soared past $100 a barrel this week.
Oman and Iran have been discussing for several weeks how to manage the crucial waterway.
The strait was free to transit before the war, but Iran now requires vessels to obtain permission and is considering a mechanism to impose service fees.
Ships that do not comply are regularly targeted by Iranian strikes, while the United States periodically bombs the Iranian coastline to challenge the Islamic republic's control of the strait.

Title: Siti Farah battles financial hurdle to military dream
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
TUMPAT: Three failed attempts at military selection have not dampened the determination of Siti Farah Damia Mohd Khairi, 20, to become a military officer.
An offer to pursue a bachelor's degree in Defence Human Resource Management at Universiti Pertahanan Nasional Malaysia (UPNM) has given the former STPM student, who achieved a 3.67 cumulative grade point average, a chance to pursue her dream.
However, she is struggling to pay the RM2,549 registration fee, which is due Sept 20.
The only child, who lost her father when she was 11 months old, said her mother, Ros Ayu Mat Ail, 44, could provide only RM1,000 for now.
"It's not just for tuition. On registration day, I also need special clothing and equipment," she said at her grandmother's house in Kampung Talak here.
Siti Farah has prepared only her daily clothing and basic necessities, though her Form 6 laptop is still usable.
Growing up without a father taught her resilience, and she hopes to repay her mother and grandmother, Siti Fatimah Omar, 75, for their sacrifices.
That determination drove her to attend every military interview she could, particularly for the air force, which has long been her passion.
"I've received three interview calls. The first time, I made it only through the initial stage. The second clashed with my Form 6 exams.
"The third call was for the navy, where I failed the physical. But these failures have not broken my spirit to keep trying.
"For now, I can only pray that I am given the means to continue my studies, as my mother sells handicraft to support us," she said.

Title: Cabinet duo trade suits for running shoes
Article:

Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil and Youth and Sports Minister Dr Mohammed Taufiq Johari took part in the run.

Title: Nestle Malaysia supports padi farmers to boost supply chain
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
JITRA: Nestle (Malaysia) Bhd has invested more than RM6 million in its Nestle Paddy Club (NPC) since 2012, as it seeks to strengthen its local rice supply chain while improving productivity and the livelihood of padi farmers.
Nestle Malaysia chief executive officer Juan Aranols said the investment also covers farming methods, agricultural inputs, machinery and technical expertise.
"It is many years of investment. I would say it's around RM6 million-plus, but the operation is not just money.
"It is also methods, practices, providing the right variety of rice and sharing all the necessary knowledge through experts," he said during a media familiarisation trip to the NPC here.
The programme currently involves about 200 farmers cultivating more than 600 hectares across Kedah and Perlis.
NPC farmers have consistently recorded yields above the national average, with some achieving an average of 5.4 tonnes per hectare in the January-February season last year and 4.96 tonnes per hectare in August-September last year, compared with the national annual average of about four tonnes per hectare.
Farmer Md Nasir Md Saman, 61, said the programme has supported him by providing technical advice, pesticides, vitamins and machinery.
He said crop losses caused by natural disasters are typically covered by the Muda Agricultural Development Authority (Mada).
"Some farmers also take out padi insurance. They pay for the insurance and if a disaster occurs, such as flooding, Mada will assess the damage and provide compensation.
"They will provide up to 50 per cent, depending on the extent of the damage," he said.
Another farmer, Zalifah Desa, 54, who has been growing padi since she was 20, said her yield has increased to about two tonnes per plot from 1.5 tonnes previously, raising her income to more than RM3,000 per plot from about RM2,000.
Nestle Malaysia has been sourcing 100 per cent of the rice used in the production of its cereal locally since 2012.
The NPC forms part of Nestle Malaysia's wider Farmer Connect programmes, which support local production of padi, chili, coffee and cocoa.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Argentina revives naval base plans
Article:
Your browser does not support the audio element.
USHUAIA: Along the Beagle Channel, an icy stretch of water at the southern tip of the Americas, lies the dormant site of the proposed Ushuaia naval base.
Earlier this month, right-wing President Javier Milei ordered that priority be given in Argentina's 2027 budget to the development of the base.
He wants it to serve as a military and logistical hub in the South Atlantic.
That message came in a speech where Milei also took a tougher line on Argentina's sovereignty claim over the British-held Falkland Islands in the South Atlantic — known in Argentina as Las Malvinas, and scene of a 1982 war between the two countries.
The Falklands lie about 560km to the northeast of Ushuaia.
The foundation stone for the Ushuaia base was laid in 2022 by the previous centre-left government in Buenos Aires, but work has since stalled.
Only about nine per cent of the project has been completed, according to a government report submitted to lawmakers in the middle of last year.
Milei, a close ally of US President Donald Trump, has previously championed development of the base in the context of Argentina's alignment with Washington.
In 2024, he declared it would be a "joint military base" with the United States, but aides walked that idea back and insisted any base would be 100 per cent Argentine — a stance reiterated by his office last week.
"One hundred per cent Argentine. There is no material collaboration from the United States to build the base," presidential spokesman Adrian Ravier said on Tuesday.
There is currently no active construction — just a 2,500sq m concrete slab on a 38ha vacant but restricted lot near the Ushuaia airport.
Milei has not offered a timeline for the base's completion.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar bestowed Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award
Article:
KOZHIKODE, India: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has received the inaugural Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award in recognition of more than five decades of public service and contributions to education, Islamic scholarship, institutional development, international dialogue and human well-being.
The award was presented during a gathering held in Anwar's honour at the Markaz Convention Centre here during his visit to at Markazu Saquafathi Sunniya, also known as Jamia Markaz, one of India's prominent Islamic institutions.
Anwar was also presented with a handwritten manuscript of Sahih al-Bukhari, one of the most authoritative collections of Hadith in Sunni Islam, in recognition of international Hadith recitation gatherings organised under the patronage of the Malaysian government over the past three years.
The manuscript was presented by India's Grand Mufti, Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad.
In a citation read during the ceremony, Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Rector Dr Roshan Nurani said Anwar had demonstrated perseverance, institutional vision and a sustained commitment to dialogue, equitable development, education and human dignity throughout his public life.
He said Anwar's contribution extended beyond political office, particularly through his efforts to preserve and disseminate the Islamic scholarly tradition.
"With profound respect, the Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation confers upon Anwar Ibrahim the first Sheikh Abu Bakar Foundation Excellence Award in recognition of his distinguished contribution to public service, education, economic and institutional development, Islamic thought and international dialogue, as well as in honour of a life dedicated to shaping society through knowledge, leadership, and service to humanity," he said.
Malaysia has also supported
international Hadith recitation gatherings
led by Sheikh Abubakr in Kuala Lumpur in 2023, 2024 and 2025, recognising the six decades of teaching and scholarship in Hadith.
Earlier,
Anwar held a meeting with Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad,
who serves as the 10th Grand Mufti of India, after attending the 18th BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Man prepares more than 100 cash-filled envelopes before death
Article:
KUALA LUMPUR: More than 100 envelopes containing cash prepared by an elderly man before his death became his final trust for his family to distribute to those who helped with his funeral arrangements.
His granddaughter, Siti Mahirah Azemi, 30, said her grandfather, Yob Abd Karim, 93, appeared to have prepared himself for death and had set aside the money to be used when the time came.
Yob, a father of six, died on Sept 5 due to old age at his home in Segari, Manjung, Perak.
The story of his final trust was later shared by Siti Mahirah on Threads after the family found more than 100 envelopes containing money that he had prepared for those who helped with his funeral arrangements.
Siti Mahirah said her grandfather had appeared ready to leave and had often said before his death that his time was near.
"Tok wan (grandfather) would always say that he was no longer strong and did not have much time left, but we did not expect that he had prepared envelopes containing money to be given to those who helped with his funeral arrangements.
"There were more than 100 envelopes, and we ourselves do not know when they were prepared because the envelopes were already old," she said when contacted yesterday.
Siti Mahirah said her father, Azemi Yob, had told her that her grandfather had informed her grandmother, Selmiah Said, 85, that he had set aside the money for those who would help with his funeral arrangements.
She added that the envelopes were given to those who helped with her grandfather's funeral arrangements as he had entrusted, but most of them did not take the money and instead returned it to the family to be donated in his name.
"So, we used it to hold a tahlil and donated it to the mosque as an ongoing charity for him," she said.
She said her grandfather did not suffer from any chronic illness, but his health began to deteriorate after he fell in the bathroom about two months ago, which limited his mobility.
Siti Mahirah said memories of her grandfather would remain etched in the family's hearts, especially the final trust he had left behind.
"Next year, we will no longer be able to celebrate Hari Raya with him, but we will always remember all his teachings and kindness," she said.

Title: 'I thought she was alone,' says sister of fish pond electrocution victim
Article:
BESUT: Wan Affida Malina Wan Awang rushed to a fish farm pond in Pantai Air Tawar here after being told that her sister, Wan Adilah, had become unconscious, believed to have suffered an electric shock.
However, the 51-year-old did not expect to find that a university student undergoing industrial training at the pond, Rubayyi Razak, 27, was also involved in the incident that claimed her sister's life.
"Initially, I thought my sister was the only one lying beside the fish pond, but it turned out there were two of them, including the trainee.
"I was about 20 metres across the pond and did not dare approach them because I was worried there might still be an electrical current," she said when met at the Forensic Unit of Besut Hospital yesterday.
Wan Affida Malina said she was informed about the incident by a family acquaintance at 1.07pm.
She said her sister, Wan Adilah, 49, was the third of seven siblings and had been managing the fish farm since 2019.
She described Wan Adilah as a cheerful and friendly person who was nevertheless firm when making decisions.
"She was also capable of managing the fish farm on her own.
"Usually, whenever there was any news or anything to share, she preferred to tell my son, Hakim, because he was the one who travelled back and forth to the pond to see her, whom we called Mak Teh," she said.
Wan Affida Malina said her two children, Muhammad Nizar Hakim Miliki, 22, and Nor Aiesyah Miliki, 25, would often help Wan Adilah at the fish farm when they were on study or work breaks.
"She was active in associations and had joined youth clubs from a young age, holding various important positions in organisations," she said, adding that she last saw her sister in person last week.
It was reported that
both women
were believed to have died after suffering electric shocks at the fish farm pond yesterday.
District police chief Superintendent Mohd Rozaime Ab Rahim was quoted as saying that police received a report about the incident at about 1.40pm after the two women were found unconscious at the pond.
The case has been classified as a sudden death report.
© New Straits Times Press (M) Bhd

Title: Anwar meets India Grand Mufti in Kerala
Article:
KOZHIKODE, India: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim met prominent Sunni Muslim cleric and Grand Mufti of India Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad at Jamia Markaz here, as Malaysia seeks to deepen religious, educational and economic ties with southern India.
Sheikh Abubakr Ahmad described the meeting as a "fruitful interaction" in a post on X.
Anwar received a warm welcome at Markaz in Karanthur, Kozhikode, where he also met prominent Sunni Muslim cleric Kanthapuram A.P. Aboobacker Musliyar.
During a private meeting with Kanthapuram, Anwar discussed educational exchanges between Markaz and Malaysian higher education institutions, potential cooperation in education, culture, knowledge and the welfare of the Indian community in Malaysia, according to ANI News.
Following the meeting, Anwar attended a dinner hosted by the Grand Mufti, which brought together prominent figures from the religious, political, social, cultural and business sectors.
The prime minister later visited the Madavoor C.M. Valiyullah Dargah, an important pilgrimage site in South India.
Anwar arrived in Kozhikode after participating in the BRICS Leaders' Summit in New Delhi, hosted by Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, as part of his working visit to India.
Keralam Chief Minister V.D. Satheesan warmly welcomed Anwar upon his arrival at Karipur Airport in Kozhikode.
Anwar, who is also Finance Minister, is accompanied on the working visit by Investment, Trade and Industry Minister Datuk Seri Johari Abdul Ghani and Human Resources Minister Datuk Seri R. Ramanan.
Before arriving in Keralam, Anwar said on social media that he expected the visit to drive progress in trade, tourism, investment, economic cooperation, education and connectivity between Malaysia and India.
Anwar's maiden visit to Keralam as prime minister is seen as an important step in strengthening Malaysia-India relations, particularly with the southern Indian states, which have strong economic, tourism and people-to-people links with Malaysia.
The Consul General of Malaysia to South India, K. Saravana Kumar, told reporters on Sunday that Kerala's expertise in Ayurveda, coupled with its growing integration of traditional medicine with modern healthcare, could
offer opportunities for Malaysia
to develop its wellness tourism sector.
Tourism also offers significant scope for deeper cooperation, he said, given the strong flow of visitors between Malaysia and southern India, particularly Kerala and Tamil Nadu.
Saravana said the prime minister's visit was expected to inject fresh momentum into Malaysia's engagement with southern India while opening opportunities to develop cooperation in areas of mutual interest.
On Monday, Anwar is scheduled to attend a private programme at Tulah Clinical Wellness, where he will stay for one night.
He will later meet Satheesan and Keralam Governor Rajendra Vishwanath Arlekar at Tulah Clinical Wellness to discuss bilateral cooperation in key sectors, including trade and investment, tourism, healthcare and education.
Anwar is also scheduled to hold one-on-one business engagements and meetings with prominent Indian industry players and corporate figures, with the discussions expected to identify new opportunities for trade, investment and commercial cooperation.
After completing his Keralam visit, Anwar is scheduled to depart for the Maldives on Sept 14.
The working visit is expected to give further impetus to the Malaysia-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership while opening opportunities to expand high-impact cooperation, particularly in trade and investment, digital technology and education.
